---
<!-- conjecture--1: body_md -->
Let $E/\bQ$ be an elliptic curve. Assume that $\mathfrak{X}_\Gr(E/\bQ_\infty)$ is $\Lambda$-torsion. Then there is an elliptic curve $E'$ in the $\bQ$-isogeny class of $E$ such that $\mu(\cL_{E'}^\Gr)=0$. Whenever $\cL_E^\MSD$ (hence $\cL_{E'}^\MSD$) is well-defined, $\mu(\cL_{E'}^\MSD)=0$ for the same $E'$.
<!-- end conjecture--1 -->
<!-- maintheorem-1: body_md -->
\label{mainthm}
    Let $E/\bQ$ be an elliptic curve, and let $p$ be an odd good ordinary Eisenstein prime for $E$. Then Greenberg's conjecture holds. When $E$ has multiplicative reduction at $p$, the algebraic part of Greenberg's conjecture holds.
<!-- end maintheorem-1 -->
<!-- maintheorem-2: body_md -->
\label{classical}
     Let $E/\bQ$ be an elliptic curve, and let $p$ be an odd ordinary Eisenstein prime for $E$. Then over the $p$-th division field $\bQ(E[p])$ of $E$, the following $\mu$-invariants vanish (see~\cref{introiwa} and~\cref{deffine} for definitions):
     \begin{itemize}
         \item[(i)] The classical $\mu$-invariant;
         \item[(ii)] The classical fine $\mu$-invariant;
         \item[(iii)] The fine $\mu$-invariant for $E$.
     \end{itemize}
<!-- end maintheorem-2 -->
<!-- maintheorem-3: body_md -->
\label{irred}
 Let $E$ be an elliptic curve and $p$ be an odd prime of ordinary reduction for $E$. Assume $E[p]$ is irreducible as a $G_\bQ$-module. Let $L=\bQ(E[p])$. Then $\mu(A^\fn_{L,\infty})=0\Rightarrow\mu(\Sel_\Gr(E/\bQ_\infty)^\vee)=0.$
<!-- end maintheorem-3 -->
<!-- conjecture--2: body_md -->
\label{equivform}
    Let $E/\bQ$ be an elliptic curve. Assume that $p$ is an ordinary prime for $E$. Then $\mu(\mathfrak{X}_\Gr(E/\bQ_\infty))=0$ in the following situations:
    \begin{itemize}
        \item $E[p]$ is an irreducible $G_\bQ$-module, or 
        \item $E[p]$ fits into a short exact sequence of $G_\bQ$-modules \begin{equation}\label{seq:E[p]}0\to \mathbf{F}(\varphi) \to E[p] \to \mathbf{F}(\psi) \to 0,\end{equation}
        where\begin{enumerate}
            \item $\varphi$ is unramified at $p$ and odd, or ramified at $p$ and even, or
            \item $\varphi$ is unramified at $p$ and even (so $\psi$ is ramified at $p$ and odd), and the extension~\eqref{seq:E[p]} is non-split.
        \end{enumerate}
    \end{itemize}
<!-- end conjecture--2 -->
<!-- example-1: body_md -->
Let $K$ be a number field, and let $K_\infty\colonequals K\bQ_\infty$ be its cyclotomic $\bZ_p$ extension. Then there is a tower $K\colonequals K_0\subset K_1\subset ...\subset K_n\subset...$ with $[K_n:K]=p^n$ and $K_\infty=\cup_n K_n$. 
    Denote by $\Cl(K_n)[p^\infty]$ the \emph{$p$-primary} part of the class group of the $n$-the layer. Then $\varprojlim_n \Cl(K_n)[p^\infty]$ is a finitely generated torsion module over $\Lambda_K\colonequals\bZ_p\llbracket\Gal(K_\infty/K) \rrbracket\simeq \bZ_p\llbracket T\rrbracket$, and one can talk about its $\mu$-invariant.
<!-- end example-1 -->
<!-- example-2: body_md -->
Let $L_\infty/K_\infty$ the maximal unramified abelian pro-$p$ extension. Denote by $A_{K,\infty}=\Gal(L_\infty/K_\infty)$. There is a canonical isomorphism $\varprojlim_n \Cl(K_n)[p^\infty]\simeq A_{K,\infty}$.
<!-- end example-2 -->
<!-- definition-1: body_md -->
Let $K$ be an algebraic extension of $\bQ$, $v$ a finite place of $K$. Let $K_v^\ur$ be the maximal unramified extension of $K_v$. Then $\Gal(K_v^\ur/K_v)\simeq G_{K_v}/I_v$ where $I_v\cong \Gal(\overline{K}_v/K_v^\ur)$ is the inertia subgroup.
<!-- end definition-1 -->
<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
Assume $K$ is a finite extension over $\bQ$ and let $\Sigma$ be any finite set of primes containing $p$. Then \begin{align*}       
    A_{K,\infty}&\cong
    \ker\big\{\ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(K^\Sigma/K_\infty,\bQ_p/\bZ_p)\to\prod_v \ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(K_{\infty,v}, \bQ_p/\bZ_p)/\ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(K_{\infty,v}^\ur/K_{\infty,v}, \bQ_p/\bZ_p)\big\}^\vee\\
    &\cong \ker\big\{\ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(K^\Sigma/K_\infty,\bQ_p/\bZ_p)\to\prod_v \ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(I_{\infty,v}, \bQ_p/\bZ_p)\big\}^\vee
    \end{align*}
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
The first isomorphism is proposition 1.6.1 of \cite{Ru00}. The second isomorphism follows from the inflation-restriction exact sequence. It is independent from the choice of $\Sigma$ by the remark below.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- remark-1: body_md -->
\label[remark]{unrawayp}
    $A_{K,\infty}$ can be identified with\begin{align*}
    \ker\big\{\ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(K^\Sigma/K_\infty,\bQ_p/\bZ_p)\to&\prod_{v\mid p}\ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(K_{\infty,v}, \bQ_p/\bZ_p)/\ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(K_{\infty,v}^\ur/K_{\infty,v}, \bQ_p/\bZ_p)\\ 
    \cdot&\prod_{v\nmid p} \ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(K_{\infty,v}, \bQ_p/\bZ_p) \big\}^\vee,
    \end{align*} since for $v\nmid p$, $\Gal(K^\ur_{\infty,v}/K_{\infty,v})$ has profinie degree prime to $p$. In other words, unramified local condition at places away from $p$ could be replaced with \emph{strict} local condition.
<!-- end remark-1 -->
<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
\label{Ferrero-Washington}
    Assume $K/\bQ$ is an abelian extension. Then $A_{K,\infty}$ is a finitely generated $\Lambda_K$-torsion module with $\mu$-invariant 0. Consequently, $A^\fn_{K,\infty}$ is a finitely generated $\Lambda_K$-torsion module with $\mu$-invariant 0.
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
The first claim is the main result of \cite{FW79}. The consequence is immediate.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- definition-2: body_md -->
Let $\widetilde{E}$ be the reduction curve of $E$ mod $p$, and let $I_{\infty,p}$ be the inertia group of $\bQ_{\infty,p}$. Define \[\Fil^+(E[p^\infty])=\ker(E[p^\infty]\to \widetilde{E}[p^\infty]),\] $\Fil^-(E[p^\infty])=E[p^\infty]/\Fil^+(E[p^\infty])$, $\Fil^+(E[p])=\Fil^+(E[p^\infty])[p]$ and $ \Fil^-(E[p])=E[p]/\Fil^+(E[p])$.
<!-- end definition-2 -->
<!-- definition-3: body_md -->
Let $\Sigma$ be the finite set of primes containing $p$ and the primes where $E$ has bad reduction. Define \[ \Sel_\Gr(E/\bQ_\infty)=\ker(\ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(\bQ^\Sigma/\bQ_\infty, E[p^\infty])\to \prod_{v\in \Sigma-p} \ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(\bQ_{\infty,v}, E[p^\infty])\times \ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(I_{\infty,p}, \Fil^-(E[p^\infty])),\] \[ \Sel^\Sigma_\Gr(E/\bQ_\infty)=\ker(\ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(\bQ^\Sigma/\bQ_\infty, E[p^\infty])\to  \ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(I_{\infty,p}, \Fil^-(E[p^\infty])),\]
    \[\Sel_\Gr(E[p]/\bQ_\infty)=\ker(\ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(\bQ^\Sigma/\bQ_\infty, E[p])\to \prod_{v\in \Sigma-p} \ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(\bQ_{\infty,v}, E[p])\times \ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(I_{\infty,p}, \Fil^-(E[p])),\]
    \[\Sel^\Sigma_\Gr(E[p]/\bQ_\infty)=\ker(\ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(\bQ^\Sigma/\bQ_\infty, E[p])\to  \ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(I_{\infty,p}, E[p])).\]
<!-- end definition-3 -->
<!-- proposition-1: body_md -->
\label[proposition]{Greenberg Selmer torsion}
    Assume $E$ has ordinary reduction at $p$. Then $\Sel_\Gr(E/\bQ_\infty)$ and $\Sel_\Gr^\Sigma(E/\bQ_\infty)$ are finitely generated $\Lambda$-cotorsion modules
<!-- end proposition-1 -->
<!-- lemma-2: body_md -->
\label[lemma]{Sigma part mu=0}
    $\prod_{v\in \Sigma-p} H^1(\bQ_{\infty,v}, E[p^\infty])^\vee$ is a $\Lambda$-torsion module with $\mu$-invariant $0$. More generally, if $K$ is a number field, $\prod_{w\mid v,v\in \Sigma-p} H^1(K_{\infty,w}, E[p^\infty])^\vee$ is a $\Lambda$-torsion module with $\mu$-invariant $0$.
<!-- end lemma-2 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
When $K=\bQ$, this is Proposition 2.4 of \cite{GV00}. The general case follows similarly from~\cite[Proposition 2]{Gr89}, since $\ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^0(K_{\infty,w},E[p^\infty])$ is $\bZ_p$-cofinitely generated for any finite extension $K/\bQ$ and $w\nmid p$. Indeed, for primes $w$ of good reduction, $\ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^0(K_{\infty,w},E[p^\infty])$ is finite, and for bad primes, it is at most of $\bZ_p$-corank $2$. Note that we have implicitly used the fact that no place can decompose infinitely along cyclotomic $\bZ_p$-extensions.
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
(\cref{Greenberg Selmer torsion})
    The first part follows from theorem 17.4 of \cite{Ka04}. Now consider the following exact sequence
    \begin{equation*}
        0\to \Sel_\Gr(E/\bQ_\infty)\to \Sel_\Gr^\Sigma(E/\bQ_\infty)\to \prod_{v\in \Sigma-p}H^1(\bQ_{\infty,v},E[p^\infty]).
    \end{equation*} The second part follows from \cref{Sigma part mu=0}.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- definition-4: body_md -->
Let $\Sigma$ be a finite set of primes containing $p$ and the primes where $E$ has bad reduction. Define \[ \Sel_\fn(E/\bQ_\infty)=\ker(\ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(\bQ^\Sigma/\bQ_\infty, E[p^\infty])\to \prod_{v\in \Sigma} \ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(\bQ_{\infty,v}, E[p^\infty])),\] \[ \Sel^\Sigma_\fn(E/\bQ_\infty)=\ker(\ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(\bQ^\Sigma/\bQ_\infty, E[p^\infty])\to  \ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(\bQ_{\infty,p}, E[p^\infty])),\]
    \[\Sel_\fn(E[p]/\bQ_\infty)=\ker(\ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(\bQ^\Sigma/\bQ_\infty, E[p])\to \prod_{v\in \Sigma} \ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(\bQ_{\infty,v}, E[p])),\]
    \[\Sel^\Sigma_\fn(E[p]/\bQ_\infty)=\ker(\ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(\bQ^\Sigma/\bQ_\infty, E[p])\to  \ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(\bQ_{\infty,p}, E[p])).\]
<!-- end definition-4 -->
<!-- proposition-2: body_md -->
\label[proposition]{fine Selmer mu=0}
    $\Sel_\fn(E/\bQ_\infty)^\vee$ and $\Sel_\fn^\Sigma(E/\bQ_\infty)^\vee$ are finitely generated $\Lambda$-torsion modules with $\mu$-invariant 0.
<!-- end proposition-2 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
\label{Coates-Sujatha}
    Let $p\geq 3$ a prime. Assume there exists a finite extension $F/\bQ$ such that \begin{enumerate}
        \item $F\subset \bQ(E[p^\infty])$.
        \item $\bQ(E[p^\infty])/F$ a pro-$p$ extension.
        \item $F_\infty:=F\bQ_\infty$ has classical Iwasawa $\mu$-invariant 0.
    \end{enumerate} Then $\Sel_\fn(E/\bQ_\infty)$ is a finitely generated $\Lambda$-cotorsion module with $\mu$-invariant 0.
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
This is Corollary 3.5 of \cite{CS05}.
<!-- end proof-5 -->
<!-- proof-6: body_md -->
(\cref{fine Selmer mu=0})
    Suppose we have a short exact sequence of $G_\bQ$-modules \[0\to \mathbf{F}(\varphi)\to E[p]\to \mathbf{F}(\psi)\to 0.\] Take $F=\bQ(\varphi,\psi)$ as in~\cref{Q(E[p])}. Then $F\subset \bQ(E[p])\subset \bQ(E[p^\infty])$ and $[\bQ(E[p]):F]=1$ or $p$. Since $\bQ(E[p^\infty])/\bQ(E[p])$ is a pro-$p$ extension, so is $\bQ(E[p^\infty])/F$. Since $F/\bQ$ is abelian. According to \cref{Ferrero-Washington}, $F_\infty$ has classical Iwasawa $\mu$-invariant 0. Therefore, by \cref{Coates-Sujatha}, $\Sel_\fn(E/\bQ_\infty)^\vee$ is a finitely generated $\Lambda$-torsion module with $\mu$-invariant 0. The second part follows from the short exact sequence  \begin{equation*}
        0\to \Sel_\fn(E/\bQ_\infty)\to \Sel_\fn^\Sigma(E/\bQ_\infty)\to \prod_{v\in \Sigma-p}H^1(\bQ_{\infty,v},E[p^\infty])
    \end{equation*} and \cref{Sigma part mu=0}.
<!-- end proof-6 -->
<!-- remark-2: body_md -->
\label[remark]{finemuK}
    A similar sequence for a general number field $K$, namely,\[
0\to \Sel_\fn(E/K_\infty)\to \Sel_\fn^\Sigma(E/K_\infty)\to \prod_{w\mid v,v\in \Sigma-p}\ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(K_{\infty,w},E[p^\infty]),
    \]
   together with~\cref{Sigma part mu=0} shows that $\corank_\Lambda(\Sel_\fn(E/K_\infty))=\corank_\Lambda(\Sel^\Sigma_\fn(E/K_\infty))$ and $\mu(\Sel_\fn(E/K_\infty)^\vee)=\mu(\Sel^\Sigma_\fn(E/K_\infty)^\vee)$.
<!-- end remark-2 -->
<!-- lemma-3: body_md -->
$\cL_E^\MSD$ is integral, i.e., $\cL_E^\MSD\in\Lambda$.
<!-- end lemma-3 -->
<!-- proof-7: body_md -->
See for example~\cite[Theorem 2.1.1]{CGS}.
<!-- end proof-7 -->
<!-- conjecture--3: body_md -->
Let $E/\bQ$ be an elliptic curve. Assume that $\mathfrak{X}_\Gr(E/\bQ_\infty)$ is $\Lambda$-torsion. Then there is an elliptic curve $E'$ in the $\bQ$-isogeny class of $E$ such that $\mu(\cL_{E'}^\Gr)=0$. Whenever $\cL_E^\MSD$ (hence $\cL_{E'}^\MSD$) is well-defined, $\mu(\cL_{E'}^\MSD)=0$ for the same $E'$.
<!-- end conjecture--3 -->
<!-- lemma-4: body_md -->
\label[lemma]{Schformula}
    Let $\varphi$ be a $\bQ$-isogeny from $E$ to $E'$ with $C\colonequals\ker(\varphi)$ fitting into the short exact sequence\[
    0\to C\to E\xrightarrow{\varphi} E'\to 0,
    \]
    so $C$ is cyclic of order $p^n$ for some $n\in\bZ^{\geq 0}$. Then \[\mu^\alg(E')=\mu^\alg(E)+\delta,
    \]
    where \begin{equation*}
        \delta=\begin{cases}
            -n&C\text{ is ramified and odd;}\\
            n&C\text{ is unramified and even;}\\
            0&otherwise.
        \end{cases}
    \end{equation*}
    Here $C$ is ramified (\emph{resp. odd}) if and only if the action of $I_p$ (\emph{resp. complex conjugation}) on $C[p]$ is non-trivial.
<!-- end lemma-4 -->
<!-- proof-8: body_md -->
See~\cite[Lemma 1]{MR2152940}.
<!-- end proof-8 -->
<!-- conjecture--4: body_md -->
Let $E/\bQ$ be an elliptic curve. Assume that $p$ is an ordinary prime for $E$. Then $\mu(\mathfrak{X}_\Gr(E/\bQ_\infty))=0$ in the following situations:
    \begin{itemize}
        \item $E[p]$ is an irreducible $G_\bQ$-module, or 
        \item $E[p]$ fits into a short exact sequence of $G_\bQ$-modules \begin{equation}\label{seq:E[p]in2}0\to \mathbf{F}(\varphi) \to E[p] \to \mathbf{F}(\psi) \to 0,\end{equation}
        where\begin{enumerate}
            \item $\varphi$ is unramified at $p$ and odd, or ramified at $p$ and even, or
            \item $\varphi$ is unramified at $p$ and even (so $\psi$ is ramified at $p$ and odd), and the extension~\eqref{seq:E[p]in2} is non-split.
        \end{enumerate}
    \end{itemize}
<!-- end conjecture--4 -->
<!-- remark-3: body_md -->
\begin{enumerate}
    \item In~\cite{GV00}, only the good ordinary case was explicitly written, although at the beginning of the text it was pointed out that the theorems apply to elliptic curves with multiplicative reductions as well. Indeed, at least on the algebraic side, the proof of $\mu_{E,\Sigma_0}^\alg=\mu_{\varphi,\Sigma_0}^\alg+\mu_{\psi,\Sigma_0}^\alg=0$ (hence $\mu_{E}^\alg=0$) goes through almost verbatim.
    \item It was also noted that (see also~\cite[section 2]{Gr89}) in the split multiplicative case, the classical Selmer group defined using Kummer image is strictly smaller than the one defined above using ordinary local conditions. But the difference only has $\lambda$-invariant $1$, corresponding to a `trivial zero', and has no $\mu$-invariant. Therefore we will stick to the ordinary Selmer groups when we refer to the algebraic part of Greenberg's conjecture.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end remark-3 -->
<!-- proposition-3: body_md -->
\label[proposition]{finemumodp}    $\mu(\Sel_\fn(E/\bQ_\infty)^\vee)=0\Leftrightarrow \mu(\Sel^\Sigma_\fn(E[p]/\bQ_\infty)^\vee)=0.$
<!-- end proposition-3 -->
<!-- proof-9: body_md -->
Consider the diagram{\footnotesize
	\begin{equation*}\begin{tikzcd}
			0 \ar[r]& \ker(\loc^\fn_{/p}) \ar[r]\ar[d]&\Sel^\Sigma_\fn(E[p]/\bQ_\infty)  \ar[r]\ar[d]&  \Sel^\Sigma_\fn(E/\bQ_\infty)[p] \ar[d] &\\
			0 \ar[r]&  \ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^0(\bQ^\Sigma/\bQ_\infty,E[p^\infty])/p\ar[r]\ar[d,"\loc^\fn_{/p}"]& \ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(\bQ^\Sigma/\bQ_\infty,E[p])\ar[r]\ar[d]& \ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(\bQ^\Sigma/\bQ_\infty,E[p^\infty])[p]
            \ar[r]\ar[d]&0\\
			0 \ar[r]& \ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^0(\bQ_{\infty,p}, E[p^\infty])/p \ar[r]\ar[d]& \ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(\bQ_{\infty,p}, E[p]) \ar[r]& \ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(\bQ_{\infty,p}, E[p^\infty])[p]\ar[r]& 0 \\
            &\coker(\loc^\fn_{/p})&&&
\end{tikzcd}\end{equation*}}
coming from the sequence\begin{equation}\label{E[p^infty]}
    0\to E[p] \to E[p^\infty] \xrightarrow{p} E[p^\infty]\to 0,\end{equation}where $\ker(\loc^\fn_{/p})$ and $\coker(\loc^\fn_{/p})$ are finite since the domain and codomain of $\loc^\fn_{/p}$ are finite. It then follows immediately from the snake lemma that $\Sel^\Sigma_\fn(E[p]/\bQ_\infty)$ is finite if and only if $\Sel^\Sigma_\fn(E/\bQ_\infty)[p]$ is finite. Since $\Sel^\Sigma_\fn(E/\bQ_\infty)$ (hence $\Sel^\Sigma_\fn(E[p]/\bQ_\infty)$) is cotorsion, the above finiteness results are equivalent to the vanishing of the corresponding $\mu$-invariants from the structure theorem. Finally, the vanishing of $\mu(\Sel_\fn^\Sigma(E/\bQ_\infty)^\vee)$ is equivalent to the vanishing of $\mu(\Sel_\fn(E/\bQ_\infty)^\vee)$ by~\cref{Sigma part mu=0} (see also~\cref{fine Selmer mu=0}).
<!-- end proof-9 -->
<!-- remark-4: body_md -->
\label[remark]{imprimK}
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item As in~\cref{finemuK}, if one replaces $\bQ_\infty$ by $K_\infty$ in the second row, and replaces $\ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^i(\bQ_{\infty,p},-)$ by $\prod_{w\mid p}\ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^i(K_{\infty,w},-)$ in the third row of the above diagram\, the same proof shows that $\mu(\Sel_\fn(E/K_\infty)^\vee)=0\Leftrightarrow \mu(\Sel^\Sigma_\fn(E[p]/K_\infty)^\vee)=0$ for a general abelian extension $K$ of $\bQ$, where the Selmer groups are known to be $\Lambda$-cotorsion.
        \item The exact same proof also shows $\mu(A^\fn_{K,\infty})=0\Leftrightarrow \mu(A[p]^{\fn,\Sigma}_{K,\infty})=0$ by replacing $E[p^\infty]$ with $\bQ_p/\bZ_p$, and $E[p]$ with $\mathbf{F}(\mathbf{1})$, taking into account (i). This works as long as $\Sigma$ contains the places above $p$.
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end remark-4 -->
<!-- proposition-4: body_md -->
\label[proposition]{Grmumodp}
$\mu(\Sel_\Gr(E/\bQ_\infty)^\vee)=0\Leftrightarrow \mu(\Sel^\Sigma_\Gr(E[p]/\bQ_\infty)^\vee)=0.$
<!-- end proposition-4 -->
<!-- proof-10: body_md -->
Consider the diagram{\footnotesize
	\begin{equation*}\begin{tikzcd}
			0 \ar[r]& \ker(\loc^\Gr_{/p}) \ar[r]\ar[d]&\Sel^\Sigma_\Gr(E[p]/\bQ_\infty)  \ar[r]\ar[d]&  \Sel^\Sigma_\Gr(E/\bQ_\infty)[p] \ar[d] &\\
			0 \ar[r]&  \ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^0(\bQ^\Sigma/\bQ_\infty,E[p^\infty])/p\ar[r]\ar[d,"\loc^\Gr_{/p}"]& \ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(\bQ^\Sigma/\bQ_\infty,E[p])\ar[r]\ar[d]& \ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(\bQ^\Sigma/\bQ_\infty,E[p^\infty])[p]
            \ar[r]\ar[d]&0\\
			0 \ar[r]& \ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^0(I_{\infty,p},\Fil^-(E[p^\infty]))/p \ar[r]\ar[d]& \ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(I_{\infty,p},\Fil^-(E[p]))\ar[r]& \ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(I_{\infty,p},\Fil^-(E[p^\infty]))[p]\ar[r]& 0 \\
            &\coker(\loc^\Gr_{/p})& &&
\end{tikzcd}\end{equation*}}
coming from the sequence~\eqref{E[p^infty]} and the sequence\begin{equation*}
    0\to \Fil^-(E[p]) \to \Fil^-(E[p^\infty]) \xrightarrow{p} \Fil^-(E[p^\infty])\to 0,\end{equation*}
    where $\ker(\loc^\Gr_{/p})$ and $\coker(\loc^\Gr_{/p})$ are finite since the domain and codomain of $\loc^\Gr_{/p}$ are finite. The rest of the proof is then identical to that of~\cref{finemumodp}.
<!-- end proof-10 -->
<!-- remark-5: body_md -->
\label[remark]{imprimclassical}
    The same proof also shows that $\mu(A_{K,\infty})=0\Leftrightarrow \mu(A[p]^\Sigma_{K,\infty})=0$ by replacing $E[p^\infty]$ and $\Fil^-(E[p^\infty])$ with $\bQ_p/\bZ_p$, and $E[p]$ and $\Fil^-(E[p])$ with $\mathbf{F}(\mathbf{1})$, taking into account~\cref{imprimK}(i). This holds for an arbitrary number field $K$ since $A_{K,\infty}$ is $\Lambda$-torsion for any $K$ from Iwasawa's theorem. Again, this holds as long as $\Sigma$ contains places above $p$.
<!-- end remark-5 -->
<!-- head-1: body_md -->
The vanishing of classical (and hence classical fine) $\mu$ follows directly from Ferrero--Washington theorem.
The vanishing of fine $\mu$ for $E$ then further follows from~\cite[Corollary 3.6]{CS05}, as $\varphi$ becomes trivial (so $E[p]$ admits a rational point) over $K\colonequals \bQ(\varphi,\psi)$, which is an abelian extension of $\bQ$. In particular, from~\cref{imprimK} and~\cref{imprimclassical}, we have\begin{itemize}
    \item $\mu(\Sel^\Sigma_\fn(E[p]/K_\infty)^\vee)=\mu(\Sel_\fn(E/K_\infty)^\vee)=0$;
    \item $\mu(A[p]^{\fn,\Sigma}_{K,\infty})=\mu(A^\fn_{K,\infty})=0$;
    \item $\mu(A[p]^\Sigma_{K,\infty})=\mu(A_{K,\infty})=0$.
\end{itemize}

\noindent
<!-- end head-1 -->
<!-- head-2: body_md -->
This follows from the following `$p$-extension principle', which also appears in Iwasawa's Riemman--Hurwitz formula ($\mu$-part only). Here we give a proof using Nakayama's lemma. We first prove it for the fine Selmer group for $E$, and the other two cases follow similarly.

\begin{proposition}
    Let $L/K$ be a $p$-extension. If $\mu(\Sel_\fn^\Sigma(E[p]/K_\infty)^\vee)=0$, then $\mu(\Sel_\fn^\Sigma(E[p]/L_\infty)^\vee)=0$
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
    Further assume that $\Sigma$ contains places of $K$ that are ramified in $L$. Let $G=\Gal(L/K)\simeq \bZ/p^n\bZ$. Then one knows the restriction map\[
    \Sel_\fn^\Sigma(E[p]/K_\infty)\xrightarrow{\res_\fn} \Sel_\fn^\Sigma(E[p]/L_\infty)^G
    \]
    has finite kernel and cokernel. Indeed, the middle vertical map in the diagram{\footnotesize
	\begin{equation*}\begin{tikzcd}
			0 \ar[r]& \ker(\res_\fn) \ar[r]\ar[d]&\ker(\res)  \ar[r]\ar[d]&  \ker(\res_p)\ar[d] &\\
			0 \ar[r]&  \Sel_\fn^\Sigma(E[p]/K_\infty)\ar[r]\ar[d,"\res_\fn"]& \ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(K^\Sigma/K_\infty,E[p])\ar[r]\ar[d,"\res"]& \im(\ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(K^\Sigma/K_\infty,E[p]))
            \ar[r]\ar[d,"\res_p"]&0\\
			0 \ar[r]& \Sel_\fn^\Sigma(E[p]/L_\infty)^G \ar[r]\ar[d]& \ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(L^\Sigma/L_\infty,E[p])^G\ar[r]\ar[d]& \prod_{l\mid w\mid p}\ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(L_{\infty,l},E[p])& \\
            &\coker(\res_\fn)\ar[r]& \coker(\res) &&
\end{tikzcd}\end{equation*}}
has finite kernel and cokernel, since from the inflation-restriction exact sequence, $\ker(\res)=\ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(G,E[p]^{G_{L_\infty}})$ and $\coker(\res)$ is contained in $\ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^2(G,E[p]^{G_{L_\infty}})$, which are both finite as $G$ and $E[p]^{G_{L_\infty}}$ are both finite. Here $\im(\ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(K^\Sigma/K_\infty,E[p]))$ detnoes $\im(\ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(K^\Sigma/K_\infty,E[p])\to \prod_{w\mid p}\ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(K_{\infty,w},E[p]))$.

Similarly, the local restriction\[
\prod_{w\mid p}\ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(K_{\infty,w},E[p])\xrightarrow{\res_p}\prod_{l\mid w\mid p}\ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(L_{\infty,l},E[p])
\]
has finite kernel, so the $\ker(\res_p)$ in the diagram is finite. Thus both $\ker(\res_\fn)$ and $\coker(\res_\fn)$ are finite from the snake lemma. Now if $\mu(\Sel_\fn^\Sigma(E[p]/K_\infty)^\vee)=0$, then $\mu((\Sel_\fn^\Sigma(E[p]/L_\infty)^G)^\vee)=0$ as well, and $(\Sel_\fn^\Sigma(E[p]/L_\infty)^G)^\vee$ is a finitely generated $\bZ_p$-module.

    Now let $A=\bZ_p[G]$ with (unique) maximal ideal $\mathfrak{m}$, and let $I_G\colonequals \ker(A\to \bZ_p)$ be the augmentation ideal of $A$. Then $I_G\subset \mathfrak{m}$ and $\bZ_p=A/I_G$. We now know that $(\Sel_\fn^\Sigma(E[p]/L_\infty)^G)^\vee=(\Sel_\fn^\Sigma(E[p]/L_\infty))^\vee_G=(\Sel_\fn^\Sigma(E[p]/L_\infty))^\vee/I_G$ is a finitely generated $A/I_G$-module, so Nakayama's lemma implies that $(\Sel_\fn^\Sigma(E[p]/L_\infty))^\vee$ is finitely generated as a $A$-module, hence it is also finitely generated as a $\bZ_p$-module. That is, $\mu((\Sel_\fn^\Sigma(E[p]/L_\infty))^\vee)=0.$
\end{proof}

Since $\bQ(E[p])/\bQ(\varphi,\psi)$ is either a $p$-extension or trivial from~\cref{Q(E[p])}, we can choose $L=\bQ(E[p])$ and $K=\bQ(\varphi,\psi)$. Then we can apply the above proposition together with step (i) and~\cref{imprimK},~\cref{imprimclassical} to conclude step (ii), that is, $\mu(\Sel_\fn(E/L_\infty)^\vee)=\mu(\Sel_\fn^\Sigma(E[p]/L_\infty)^\vee)=0$. Finally, the above argument still works if one replaces $E[p]$ by $\mathbf{F}(\mathbf{1})$, and decomposition groups by inertia groups, so $\mu(A^\fn_{L,\infty})=\mu(A[p]^{\fn,\Sigma}_{L,\infty})=0$ and $\mu(A_{L,\infty})=\mu(A[p]^\Sigma_{L,\infty})=0$ as well.
<!-- end head-2 -->
<!-- proposition-5: body_md -->
Let $L/K$ be a $p$-extension. If $\mu(\Sel_\fn^\Sigma(E[p]/K_\infty)^\vee)=0$, then $\mu(\Sel_\fn^\Sigma(E[p]/L_\infty)^\vee)=0$
<!-- end proposition-5 -->
<!-- proof-11: body_md -->
Further assume that $\Sigma$ contains places of $K$ that are ramified in $L$. Let $G=\Gal(L/K)\simeq \bZ/p^n\bZ$. Then one knows the restriction map\[
    \Sel_\fn^\Sigma(E[p]/K_\infty)\xrightarrow{\res_\fn} \Sel_\fn^\Sigma(E[p]/L_\infty)^G
    \]
    has finite kernel and cokernel. Indeed, the middle vertical map in the diagram{\footnotesize
	\begin{equation*}\begin{tikzcd}
			0 \ar[r]& \ker(\res_\fn) \ar[r]\ar[d]&\ker(\res)  \ar[r]\ar[d]&  \ker(\res_p)\ar[d] &\\
			0 \ar[r]&  \Sel_\fn^\Sigma(E[p]/K_\infty)\ar[r]\ar[d,"\res_\fn"]& \ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(K^\Sigma/K_\infty,E[p])\ar[r]\ar[d,"\res"]& \im(\ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(K^\Sigma/K_\infty,E[p]))
            \ar[r]\ar[d,"\res_p"]&0\\
			0 \ar[r]& \Sel_\fn^\Sigma(E[p]/L_\infty)^G \ar[r]\ar[d]& \ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(L^\Sigma/L_\infty,E[p])^G\ar[r]\ar[d]& \prod_{l\mid w\mid p}\ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(L_{\infty,l},E[p])& \\
            &\coker(\res_\fn)\ar[r]& \coker(\res) &&
\end{tikzcd}\end{equation*}}
has finite kernel and cokernel, since from the inflation-restriction exact sequence, $\ker(\res)=\ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(G,E[p]^{G_{L_\infty}})$ and $\coker(\res)$ is contained in $\ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^2(G,E[p]^{G_{L_\infty}})$, which are both finite as $G$ and $E[p]^{G_{L_\infty}}$ are both finite. Here $\im(\ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(K^\Sigma/K_\infty,E[p]))$ detnoes $\im(\ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(K^\Sigma/K_\infty,E[p])\to \prod_{w\mid p}\ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(K_{\infty,w},E[p]))$.

Similarly, the local restriction\[
\prod_{w\mid p}\ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(K_{\infty,w},E[p])\xrightarrow{\res_p}\prod_{l\mid w\mid p}\ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(L_{\infty,l},E[p])
\]
has finite kernel, so the $\ker(\res_p)$ in the diagram is finite. Thus both $\ker(\res_\fn)$ and $\coker(\res_\fn)$ are finite from the snake lemma. Now if $\mu(\Sel_\fn^\Sigma(E[p]/K_\infty)^\vee)=0$, then $\mu((\Sel_\fn^\Sigma(E[p]/L_\infty)^G)^\vee)=0$ as well, and $(\Sel_\fn^\Sigma(E[p]/L_\infty)^G)^\vee$ is a finitely generated $\bZ_p$-module.

    Now let $A=\bZ_p[G]$ with (unique) maximal ideal $\mathfrak{m}$, and let $I_G\colonequals \ker(A\to \bZ_p)$ be the augmentation ideal of $A$. Then $I_G\subset \mathfrak{m}$ and $\bZ_p=A/I_G$. We now know that $(\Sel_\fn^\Sigma(E[p]/L_\infty)^G)^\vee=(\Sel_\fn^\Sigma(E[p]/L_\infty))^\vee_G=(\Sel_\fn^\Sigma(E[p]/L_\infty))^\vee/I_G$ is a finitely generated $A/I_G$-module, so Nakayama's lemma implies that $(\Sel_\fn^\Sigma(E[p]/L_\infty))^\vee$ is finitely generated as a $A$-module, hence it is also finitely generated as a $\bZ_p$-module. That is, $\mu((\Sel_\fn^\Sigma(E[p]/L_\infty))^\vee)=0.$
<!-- end proof-11 -->
<!-- head-3: body_md -->
This is where we use the non-splitness of~\eqref{seq:E[p]}. Since the sequence\[
0\to \ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^0(L^\Sigma/L_\infty,\mathbf{F}(\psi))\to\ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^0(L^\Sigma/L_\infty,E[p])\to\ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^0(L^\Sigma/L_\infty,\mathbf{F}(\varphi))\to 0
\]is exact (using spliness of $E[p]$ over $L$, as the actions are all trivial and they obtain maximal invariants of sizes $p$, $p^2$ and $p$ respectively), $\ker(\proj_L)$ is given by $\ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(L^\Sigma/L_\infty,\mathbf{F}(\psi))$. The finiteness of $\ker(\proj_L\circ\res_{L/\bQ})$ is then equivalent to the finiteness of $\im(\res_{L/\bQ})\cap \ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(L^\Sigma/L_\infty,\mathbf{F}(\psi))$.

Note that $\im(\res_{L/\bQ})$ lies in $\ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(L^\Sigma/L_\infty,E[p])^{\Gal(L_\infty/\bQ_\infty)}$. If the intersection $\im(\res_{L/\bQ})\cap \ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(L^\Sigma/L_\infty,\mathbf{F}(\psi))$ was infinite, $\ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(L^\Sigma/L_\infty, \mathbf{F}(\psi))$ would admit an infinite $\Gal(L_\infty/\bQ_\infty)$-invariant subspace. We will show that this is not possible.

Since~\eqref{seq:E[p]} is non-split over $G_\bQ$ and $G_L$ acts trivially on $E[p]$,~\eqref{seq:E[p]} remains non-split over $\Gal(L/\bQ)$ and $\mathbf{F}(\psi)$ is not a $\Gal(L/\bQ)$-invariant submodule. In other words, if we denote by $\rho_E:\Gal(L/\bQ)\to \Aut(E[p])$ the Galois action on $E[p]$ and assume $P$ is a generator of $\mathbf{F}(\psi)$, then there exists $\sigma\in \Gal(L/\bQ)$ such that $\rho_E(\sigma)(P)\notin \mathbf{F}(\psi)$. In the following, we identify $\Gal(L_\infty/\bQ_\infty)\simeq \Gal(L/\bQ)$ since $L\cap\bQ_\infty=\bQ$. Indeed, if not, by a field degree comparison we see that $L\cap\bQ_\infty$ is at most (and will be) $\bQ_1$, the first layer in $\bQ_\infty$. But then $\bQ(E[p])$ must be a strict $p$-extension of $\bQ(\varphi,\psi)$ while being equal to $\bQ(\varphi,\psi)\bQ_1$. The former is not abelian over $\bQ$ but the latter is. Contradiction arises.

Now assume by contradiction that the intersection of the image of $\ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(\bQ^\Sigma/\bQ_\infty, E[p])$ in $\ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(L^\Sigma/L_\infty, E[p])$ and $\ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(L^\Sigma/L_\infty, \mathbf{F}(\psi))$ was infinite. Then there exists a nontrivial $ f\in \ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(L^\Sigma/L_\infty,\mathbf{F}(\psi))=\Hom(\Gal(L^\Sigma/L_\infty), \mathbf{F}(\psi))$ that is $\Gal(L_\infty/\bQ_\infty)=\Gal(L/\bQ)$-invariant. Since $f$ is nontrivial, there exists $\tau\in \Gal(L^\Sigma/L_\infty)$ such that $f(\tau)=P$. However, $(\sigma\cdot f )(\tau)=\sigma(f(\sigma^{-1}\tau \sigma))=\sigma(f(\tau))=\sigma(P)\notin \mathbf{F}(\psi)$, contradicting the invariance $\sigma\cdot f=f$. Therefore, the image must be finite, and in fact, trivial.

Finally, the finiteness of $\ker(\res_{L/\bQ})$ follows from the inflation restriction exact sequence, as both $[L:\bQ]$ and the coefficient $E[p]$ are finite.

\noindent
<!-- end head-3 -->
<!-- head-4: body_md -->
From the definitions, $\ker(\loc_{L,\mathbf{F}(\varphi)})^\vee$ is nothing but $A[p]^{\fn,\Sigma}_{L,\infty}$. Thus the result follows from~\cref{Ferrero-Washington} and~\cref{imprimK}.
<!-- end head-4 -->
<!-- theorem-3: body_md -->
Let $E/\bQ$ be an elliptic curve and let $p$ be an odd prime of good ordinary reduction for $E$. Assume that $E$ admits a rational $p$-isogeny, i.e., $p$ is an \emph{Eisenstein} prime for $E$. Then the Iwasawa Main Conjecture holds for $E$ at $p$, i.e.,\[
    \Char_\Lambda(\mathfrak{X}_{\Gr}(E/\bQ_\infty))=(\cL_E^\MSD)\text{ in }\Lambda.
    \]
<!-- end theorem-3 -->
<!-- proof-12: body_md -->
The theorem was first proved in~\cite{GV00} in case (i) of~\eqref{seq:E[p]in2}. Using a different method,~\cite{CGS} proved it in all cases assuming $\varphi|_{G_p}\ne\mathbf{1}$ or $\omega$. The last hypothesis was removed in~\cite{KY24}.
<!-- end proof-12 -->
<!-- corollary-1: body_md -->
\label[corollary]{alg=anmu}
    Let $E/\bQ$ be an elliptic curve and let $p$ be an odd prime of good ordinary reduction for $E$. Assume that $E$ admits a rational $p$-isogeny, i.e., $p$ is an \emph{Eisenstein} prime for $E$. Then \[
    \mu^\alg(E)=\mu^\an(E),
    \]
    that is, the algebraic $\mu$-invariant of $E$ agrees with its analytic $\mu$-invariant.
<!-- end corollary-1 -->
<!-- theorem-4: body_md -->
Let $E/\bQ$ be an elliptic curve and let $p$ be an odd Eisenstein prime of good ordinary reduction for $E$. Let $E_\min$ be the minimal curve in the isogeny class of $E$ in the sense of Stevens~\cite{Stevens}. Then $\mu^\an(E_\min)=\mu^\alg(E_\min)=0$.
<!-- end theorem-4 -->
<!-- proof-13: body_md -->
This is a combination of~\cref{mainthm},~\cref{alg=anmu} and Schneider's formula (namely~\cref{Schformula} and~\cite[Proposition (4.12)]{Stevens}).
<!-- end proof-13 -->
<!-- theorem-5: body_md -->
Let $E$ be an elliptic curve and $p$ be an odd prime of ordinary reduction for $E$. Assume $E[p]$ is irreducible as a $G_\bQ$-module. Let $L=\bQ(E[p])$. Enlarge $\Sigma$ to include primes ramified in $L$. Then $\mu(A^\fn_{L,\infty})=0\Rightarrow$ $\Sel_\fn(E/L_\infty)$ is $\Lambda_L$-cotorsion with $\mu=0$, and $\mu(\Sel_\Gr(E/\bQ_\infty)^\vee)=0.$
<!-- end theorem-5 -->
<!-- proof-14: body_md -->
Let's consider again the extended diagram with\begin{center}{\small\begin{equation*}\begin{tikzcd}	
			 \ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(\bQ^\Sigma/\bQ_\infty,E[p]) \ar[r,"\res_{L/\bQ}"]\ar[d,"loc_\bQ"]& \ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(L^\Sigma/L_\infty,E[p])\ar[d,"loc_{L}"]\ar[r,"\proj_L"] &\ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(L^\Sigma/L_\infty,\mathbf{F}(\varphi))\ar[d,"\loc_{L,\mathbf{F}(\varphi)}"]\\
			 \ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(\bQ_{\infty,p},E[p])\ar[r,"\prod_{w_i\mid p}\res"]&\prod_{w_i\mid p}\ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(L_{\infty,w_i},E[p])\ar[r,"\prod \proj_i"]&\prod_{w_i\mid p}\ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(L_{\infty,w_i},\mathbf{F}(\varphi)),\\	 	\end{tikzcd}
             \end{equation*}}
\end{center}
where the splitting of $E[p]$ over $L$ remains true. In this case, globally $\mathbf{F}(\psi)$ is defined as the fixed $\mathbf{F}$-line in $E[p]$ that carries the $G_{\bQ_p}$ action of $\varphi$, which is not a $G_\bQ$-submodule by irreducibility, which becomes a $G_L$-submodule of $E[p]$, with a quotient denoted by $\mathbf{F}(\psi)$. The splitting of $E[p]$ over $\bQ_p$ was never used, and merely that $\mathbf{F}(\psi)$ is a sub was necessary. 

First, $\mu(A^\fn_{L,\infty})=0$ implies that $\Sel_\fn^\Sigma(E/L_\infty)$ (and hence $\Sel_\fn(E/L_\infty)$) is $\Lambda_L$-cotorsion, and that $\mu(\Sel_\fn(E/L_\infty)^\vee)=\mu(\Sel^\Sigma_\fn(E[p]/L_\infty)^\vee)$ is $0$, for any $\Sigma$ containing places above $p$ and those where $E$ has bad reduction. Indeed, from the following diagram (everything trivializes over $L$){\footnotesize
	\begin{equation*}\begin{tikzcd}
			0 \ar[r]& \Sel_\fn^\Sigma(\mathbf{F}(\mathbf{1})/L_\infty) \ar[r]\ar[d]&\Sel^\Sigma_\fn(E[p]/L_\infty)  \ar[r]\ar[d]&  \Sel^\Sigma_\fn(\mathbf{F}(\mathbf{1})/L_\infty) \ar[d] &\\
			0 \ar[r]&  \ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(L^\Sigma/L_\infty,\mathbf{F}(\mathbf{1}))\ar[r]\ar[d,"\loc^\Gr_{/p}"]& \ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(L^\Sigma/L_\infty,E[p])\ar[r]\ar[d]& \ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(L^\Sigma/L_\infty,\mathbf{F}(\mathbf{1}))
            \ar[r]\ar[d]&0\\
			0 \ar[r]& \prod_{w\mid p}\ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(L_{\infty,w},\mathbf{F}(\mathbf{1})) \ar[r]& \prod_{w\mid p}\ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(L_{\infty,w},E[p])\ar[r]& \prod_{w\mid p}\ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(L_{\infty,w},\mathbf{F}(\mathbf{1}))\ar[r]& 0,
\end{tikzcd}\end{equation*}}
it is easy to see that in fact $\mu(A[p]^{\fn,\Sigma}_{L,\infty})=0$ if and only if $\mu(\Sel^\Sigma_\fn(E[p]/L_\infty)^\vee)=0$, but the former is equivalent to the assumption $\mu(A^\fn_{L,\infty})=0$, so in fact $\Sel^\Sigma_\fn(E[p]/L_\infty)$ is finite. The structure theorem then implies that $\Sel^\Sigma_\fn(E/L_\infty)$ is $\Lambda_L$-cotorsion with $\mu$-invariant $0$. So the same holds for $\Sel_\fn(E/L_\infty)$. Moreover, $\Sel^\Sigma_\fn(E[p]/\bQ_\infty)$ is finite as well. Thus $\mu(\Sel_\fn(E/\bQ_\infty)^\vee)=0$. What we need to show next is that no global $\mu$-factor lands fully in $\ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(\bQ_\infty, \mathbf{F}(\psi))$. It suffices to show $\ker(\loc_{L,\mathbf{F}(\varphi)}\circ \proj_L\circ \res_{L/\bQ})$ is finite. As before, it suffices to show $\ker(\loc_{L,\mathbf{F}(\varphi)})$ is finite and $\ker(\proj_L\circ \res_{L/\bQ})$ is finite. The former follows from the assumption that $\mu(A^\fn_{L,\infty})=0$ (and that its torsion) by~\cref{imprimK}, and the latter is again equivalent to the finiteness of $\im(\res_{L/\bQ})\cap \ensuremath{\text{\textup{H}}}^1(L^\Sigma/L_\infty, \mathbf{F}(\psi))$.

Again, as in the non-split Eisenstein case, $\mathbf{F}(\psi)$ is not $\Gal(L/\bQ)$-invariant. The same argument as in~\cref{proofmain} shows that this kernel must indeed be finite, as $L=\bQ(E[p])$ and $\bQ_\infty$ are still linearly disjoint.
<!-- end proof-14 -->
